text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Opposition coalition Zajedno supporters continue protests in Belgrade which have been staged for over a month every day now.
- The initative board of the Student protest 96 addressed a letter to Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic holding him most responsible for the "outcome of this legal-political farce".
- Serbian police issues warning that it will no longer allow arbitrary blockade of traffic and warns organisers of the demonstrations to abide by regulations regarding protests.
- Peaceful protests will continue despite bans, says Zoran Djindjic, president of Democratic Party, one of the coalition Zajedno members.
- The Serbian parliament adopts 1997 budget of 14,65 billion dinars and passes law on labour relations.

- It is probably true that part of the country's foreign currency assets were transferred abroad while the country was under sanctions but now the National bank of Yugoslavia and the federal government have ordered checking all funds taken out of the country and putting them in the function of foreign currency reserves, said Serbian finance minister Dusan Vlatkovic.
- Independent trade union of City Transport Company (GSP) announced it would start a strike Thursday because the government has failed to respond to its wage increase demands filed ten days earlier.
- Yugoslav construction firms complete in Moscow the construction of the building of Sberbank, Russia's biggest bank, worth over $12.5 million.

- The Belgrade weekly Ekonomska Politika draws up a list of YUgoslavia's top 200 firms in 1995 with Hydroelectric power plant Djerdap in Kladovo, Thermoelectric power plant Nikola Tesla in Obrenovac and Serbian Oil Industry NIS in Novi Sad as first three.
- Textile and leather producers ask for better conditions for export of their products.

- The banking sector's insolvency is not alarming even though it is far from the favourable situation at the end of the summer when the rserve requirement was intoduced, says a source at the National Bank of Yugoslavia.
- Montenegrin parliament adopts 1997 budget at 1.99 billion dinars.
- According to latest information 58 persons were admitted in the Belgrade emergency hospital following the Tuesday demonstrations.
- Pancevo petrochemicals factory Petrohemija now operates with 90 percent capacity and plans to operate with 97 percent capacity next year and earn $270 million, says general manager Slobodan Tresac.
